note: National animal: tiger (Panthera tigris), Indian race = Royal Bengal Tiger; Project Tiger launched April 1973 (MEA/india.gov.in text, claim c23/c24). The bank item's '27 tiger reserves' figure is out of date in the source and is deliberately NOT taught (disclosed in the section deep text).
National bird: Indian peacock, Pavo cristatus (claim c25); protection under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 also taught (c26).
Jana-gana-mana: composed originally in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore, adopted in its Hindi version by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950 (claim c13).
Vande Mataram: composed in Sanskrit by Bankimchandra Chatterji, inspiration in the freedom struggle, equal status with Jana-gana-mana (claims c16, c20).
State Emblem: adaptation of the Sarnath Lion Capital; motto Satyameva Jayate in Devanagari; adopted 26 January 1950 (claims c06, c08, c10).
National calendar: Saka Era based, Chaitra first month, normal year 365 days, adopted from 22 March 1957; 1 Chaitra = 22 March normally, 21 March in a leap year (claims c21, c22).
National aquatic animal: Gangetic river dolphin; NGRBA first meeting 5 October 2009 decision (PIB relid 55824, claim c29) and designation confirmed by PIB PRID 1946399 (claim c28).

National River: Ganga — taught from the National Mission for Clean Ganga's own page title/heading 'Ganga-A National River' (claim c30). Sourcing is thinner than for the other symbols (no narrative paragraph on the fetched page), disclosed in REPORT.md.
Flag panels (saffron top, green bottom, white middle) and Ashoka Chakra in navy blue with 24 equally spaced spokes (claims c01, c03, c05).

Ratio 3:2 (length:height) taught from both the MEA text and the Flag Code FAQ (claims c02, c32). Partial: the bank item's standard-size table (450x300 mm aircraft, 225x150 mm motor-car, 150x100 mm table flags) is NOT taught — the fetched Flag Code FAQ does not list sizes; only the BIS nine-sizes fact (IS 1-1968) is taught (c37).
Design of the National Flag adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947 (claims c04, c05); the item's secondary PIB quotes about the Constitution/anthem are covered under c38/c13.

Meaning of the flag's colours and wheel in Dr. Radhakrishnan's interpretation (saffron = renunciation, white = path of truth, green = relation to soil, wheel = law of dharma): NOT taught. The interpretation text exists only in the MHA Flag Code PDF, which could not be fetched from this machine (both known MHA URLs returned 404); no other fetched official page carries it. Left untaught rather than written from memory; flagged in the flag section's deep text.

Flag Code of India, 2002: took effect 26 January 2002 and governs display together with the Emblems and Names Act, 1950 framework and the Prevention of Insults Act, 1971 (claim c31, PIB FAQ PRID 1845264). Partial: the Code's three-part division is not stated in the fetched FAQ text and is not asserted in the chapter.
Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, section 2: insult to the National Flag punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both (claim c35, MHA Act PDF fetched in full).
Emblem profile: three lions, Dharma Chakra in the centre, bull on the right, galloping horse on the left, bell-shaped lotus omitted (claims c08, c09 — MEA text and the Schedule to the 2005 Act).

State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005 (No. 50 of 2005, 20 December 2005); section 3 contravention punishable up to two years' imprisonment or fine up to five thousand rupees or both (claims c11, c12 — Gazette copy of the Act fetched via Karnataka DPAL).
National Anthem: first stanza of Tagore's song is the Anthem; full version playing time approximately 52 seconds; short version (first and last lines) about 20 seconds (claims c14, c15).
Vande Mataram first sung at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress — by Rabindranath Tagore (claims c16, c18).

Vande Mataram first published in Bangadarshan on 7 November 1875; incorporated in Anandamath (1882); first used as a political slogan on 7 August 1905 (claims c17, c19 — PIB 150-years backgrounder, fetched in full).

Equal status: Dr. Rajendra Prasad's Constituent Assembly statement of 24 January 1950 that Vande Mataram shall be honoured equally with Jana Gana Mana (claim c20, PIB backgrounder quoting the statement verbatim).
Real exam item (WBCS Prelims 2019, Q182): at which Congress session was Vande Mataram sung for the first time — 1896 session (claims c16, c18).
Real exam item (WBPSC Clerkship 2006, Q33): who composed Vande Mataram — Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (claims c16, c17).

Real exam item (WBCS Prelims 2017, Q60): which authority ordered playing of the National Anthem in all cinema halls (Supreme Court order of 30 November 2016). NOT taught: no fetched official source in this chapter covers the court order; the chapter teaches the Anthem itself and the 1971 Act only.

Real exam item (WBCS Prelims 2021, Q160): who designed the first Indian national flag (key: Sister Nivedita, c. 1906). NOT taught: the chapter teaches only the adopted 1947 design from official sources; the pre-1947 flag-design history is not in any fetched source.

Real exam item (WBPSC Miscellaneous Prelims 2023, Q37): who wrote the national anthems of two countries (Rabindranath Tagore — India and Bangladesh). NOT taught as asked: the chapter teaches Tagore as author of India's Anthem (c13), but the Bangladesh anthem ('Amar Sonar Bangla') fact is not in any fetched source, so the two-countries claim is not asserted.
